title: Add Any Vectors: Components Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A ladder, a kite string, a ramp: every slanted line hides an x part and a y part. Aarav crosses the college ground in two legs, 20 m one way and then 15 m another. How far from the start is he, and in which direction? Drawing it to scale is slow; components give the answer in seconds. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we add and subtract vectors by components.

On a live sim, leg B turns while the x parts stack on the x axis and the y parts stack on the y axis, the resultant R is drawn from the sums, and a graph tracks the size of R, with a slow-mo replay as Bx turns negative. We derive Rx = Ax + Bx and Ry = Ay + By step by step, then the size from Pythagoras and the angle from tan theta with quadrant care. A + B and A - B side by side, two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with two bicycle rides, the exam trap of reading the angle from tan theta in the wrong quadrant, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A ladder, a kite string, a ramp
0:26 Quick reminder: an x part and a y part
0:41 Live sim: two legs, parts stack on each axis
1:25 The rule: Rx = Ax + Bx, Ry = Ay + By
2:08 A + B vs A - B + pause and think
2:49 Which quadrant is R in? + pause and think
3:23 Worked example: two bicycle rides
4:07 Exam trap: the angle from tan theta
4:34 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:19 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Motion in Two Dimensions. Velocity and acceleration have x and y parts too.
